ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that point $P$ is a point on diagonal $BD$ of square $ABCD$, and $AP=3$, $PF \perp CD$ at point $F$, $PE \perp BC$ at point $E$. When connecting $EF$, what is the length of $EF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Let's connect CP.\\
Since square ABCD,\\
thus $\angle C=90^\circ$, AB=BC, and $\angle ABP=\angle CBP=45^\circ$. Let's connect CP again,\\
In $\triangle ABP$ and $\triangle CBP$\\
\[\left\{\begin{array}{l}
AB=BC\\
\angle ABP=\angle CBP\\
BP=BP
\end{array}\right.\]\\
thus $\triangle ABP\cong \triangle CBP$ (SAS)\\
thus AP=CP=3\\
Since PF$\perp$CD, and PE$\perp$BC,\\
thus $\angle PFC=\angle PEC=90^\circ$,\\
thus quadrilateral CEPF is a rectangle,\\
thus EF=PC=\boxed{3}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is square ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; diagonal BD connects from B to D, and point P is located on BD. Through P, draw PE downward perpendicular to BC, with foot E; through P, draw PF to the right perpendicular to CD, with foot F; what is connected in the figure is EF. Reasoning: Connect CP. Because ABCD is a square, AB = BC, and diagonal BD bisects ∠ABC, so when P is on BD, ∠ABP = ∠CBP. Also BP is a common side, so triangle ABP and triangle CBP are congruent by SAS. Therefore AP = CP. It is known that AP = 3, so CP = 3. Also PE ⟂ BC, PF ⟂ CD, and BC ⟂ CD, therefore CE, EP, PF, FC form rectangle CEPF. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, and EF and CP are the two diagonals of rectangle CEPF, so EF = CP = 3.
